In [[mathematics]] &mdash; specifically, in [[complex analysis]] &mdash; the '''Berezin transform''' is an [[integral operator]] acting on functions defined on the [[open set|open]] [[unit disk]] ''D'' of the [[complex plane]] '''C'''. Formally, for a function ''ƒ''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''D''&nbsp;→&nbsp;'''C''', the '''Berezin transform''' of ''ƒ'' is a new function ''Bƒ''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''D''&nbsp;→&nbsp;'''C''' defined at a point ''z''&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''D'' by

:<math>(B f)(z) = \int_D \frac{(1 - |z|^2)^2}{| 1 - z \bar{w} |^4} f(w) \, \mathrm{d}A (w),</math>

where {{overline|''w''}} denotes the [[complex conjugate]] of ''w'' and <math>\mathrm{d}A</math> is the area measure. It is named after [[Felix Alexandrovich Berezin]].
